frank: heads-up — examples/edge-starter is failing in the preview sandbox: `TypeError: handler.default is not a function`. Local run with ts-node is fine.

anya: that usually means the bundle emitted CJS-style interop. Which bundler + tsconfig?

frank: tsup (esbuild) with format: 'esm', target: 'es2022', platform: 'browser'. tsconfig uses moduleResolution: 'Bundler'.

pete: two problems we've seen together: (1) runtime ESM/CJS interop injected by esbuild (`__toESM` / `exports.default`) breaks strict edge loaders; (2) TS overloads+generics in our SDK cause bad inference so DX suffers.

michelle: show the SDK signature.

frank: ```ts
export function serve<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Resp<T>>;
export function serve<T extends string | number>(opts: { model: string; input: T; stream?: boolean }): Promise<Resp<T>>;
```

frank: VSCode often picks the second overload and `T` collapses, losing object inference. completions are awful.

pete: overload ordering matters — TS picks the first compatible overload for inference. Put the object-specific overload first or add a permissive fallback `T = any` as last overload for DX.

anya: runtime: avoid default export for the worker entry. Do `export const handler = ...` and point worker to `file.handler`. That sidesteps default import wrappers from bundlers.

michelle: also, set tsup/esbuild to `platform: 'neutral'`, `format: 'esm'`, `bundle: true` and ensure `package.json` in the sample has `type: "module"`. If you still see `__toESM` or `exports.default` in the built file grep for those strings; they indicate interop helpers.

frank: good call. I'll switch to named handler and try `moduleResolution: 'NodeNext'` in a dedicated `tsconfig.edge.json` (module: 'ESNext', skipLibCheck: false) so the sample mirrors Node ESM semantics.

pete: for types: keep strict internal signatures and export a public ergonomics facade, e.g.:
```ts
export function serveStrict<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Resp<T>>;
export function serve<T = any>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Resp<T>>; // public convenience
```
Document why we do that and add a tiny VSCode completion smoke test to CI.

michelle: also add a short README in the sample explaining: named-only entry exports, tsconfig.edge.json, bundler flags snippet, and a checklist for edge onboarding. Include a rollup example for customers using rollup.

ci-bot: preview build: examples/edge-starter failed (worker-lint).

frank: I'll open a small PR with: - swap default -> named handler - add tsconfig.edge.json - reorder/add fallback overload - README + checklist. Will tag @devex when ready. Thanks!
